uBg.title: Background / cloud agent
uBg.body:
Hand the task to the cloud: it works alone on a copy of the code and hands back a branch or a pull request (PR).

📍 Location: App overview › Using agents › Let it run alone › Background / cloud agent
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it

🎯 Role

  • Each task gets an isolated sandbox: installing, editing, testing never touch your computer.
  • You can run several at once without interference.

▶ How to use it

  • Write down what to change and what counts as done (e.g. “these tests must pass”).
  • Review the PR as you would a colleague’s: read the diff and test results, then decide whether to merge.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

“Copy + branch + review” lets it try freely: the worst case is that you do not merge.

✅ Why this works

Hand off a queue of small jobs; you only spend review time.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Needs a clear task and tests; jobs that need frequent decisions do not fit.

uRoutine.title: Routines & automation
uRoutine.body:
No need to ask: on a schedule or when something happens, the agent runs a fixed prompt automatically.

📍 Location: App overview › Using agents › Let it run alone › Routines & automation
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it

🎯 Role

  • Triggers: a schedule (9 am daily) or an event (a new email, a new ticket, a new commit).
  • Each run is “fixed prompt + fixed tools + new data”.

▶ How to use it

  • Make the output checkable: keep logs, write a report or a draft.
  • Irreversible actions (sending, deleting, paying) produce a draft first; a person approves before they happen.
  • Make it idempotent: running twice on the same thing has the effect of once (e.g. check whether it was already done).

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Nobody is beside it, so “spot and undo mistakes” has to be designed in.

✅ Why this works

Repetitive work runs by itself; you look only at results and exceptions.

⚠️ Limits / notes: It will not notice if the prompt or data drifts; check the logs regularly.

uMulti.title: Multi-agent teams
uMulti.body:
A coordinator splits a big task, sends parts to several workers in parallel, and a reviewer checks and merges the results.

📍 Location: App overview › Using agents › Let it run alone › Multi-agent teams
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it

🎯 Role

  • Each sub-agent has its own context and only sees its part.
  • Fits work that splits into independent parts, e.g. researching several directions at once.

▶ How to use it

  • Give each worker a complete brief: it cannot see the coordinator’s conversation.
  • Always end with a “merge and check” step.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

One context window cannot hold everything; split up, each sub-agent’s context is cleaner, and they run in parallel.

✅ Why this works

Big tasks finish faster, and each part is done better.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Costs more (several contexts, more calls); when parts depend on each other, coordination eats the benefit.
